title: Scripture: justified by faith; theologians dispute the sense
source_text: I. Nos fide, per fidem, & ex fide justificari, Scriptura ita diserte & frequenter inculcat, ut nemo Christianus hac de re dubitare possit. Sed non consentiunt inter se Theologi, qua ratione id sit intelligendum, & quo sensu justificatio hominis peccatoris a Spiritu Sancto fidei tribuatur. Resque est quam multum obscurant Theologorum disputationes, & magna contentione agitatae controversiae, quibus aliquid lucis, quantum Deus dabit, afferre est animus.
pass_a_gloss: Scripture so clearly and often presses that we are justified by faith, through faith, and from faith that no Christian can doubt it. Yet theologians do not agree among themselves by what reason this is to be understood, and in what sense the Holy Spirit attributes the justification of a sinful man to faith. The matter is one that the disputations of theologians greatly obscure, and controversies agitated with great contention—to which it is our intent to bring some light, as much as God will give.
pass_b_english: Scripture plainly says we are justified by / through / from faith.
Theologians still dispute the sense; this tract seeks clarity amid the clash.
